en: Jātaka:
The Section of Sevens, Chapter on the Hen-Fowl (Kukkuvagga)
7. The Sattubhasta Jātaka:
“Your mind is distracted and your senses are agitated;
from your eyes, streams of water flow.”
“What have you lost, or what do you desire, that you have come here, O Brahmā? Pray tell me this.
“My wife would die today, as I am departing.”
“The spirit spoke of death approaching;
I am trembling because of this suffering.
Tell me the meaning of this, Senaka.”
“Having reflected upon many points,
that which I shall say here is the truth alone;
I consider you, O Brahmin, to be like a bag of grain.”
A black snake has entered while you were unaware.
Take up your staff and strike it—
the bag-like, blind, deaf, double-tongued serpent!
"Cut through your doubt and your hesitations;
see the serpent and let go of the bellows.
Thus, appearing deeply moved in the midst of the assembly, he spoke.
Then the brahmin released the bag of poison;
thereupon a serpent emerged,
a venomous snake of fierce power, spreading its hood.
“Great gain has been obtained by King Janaka,
who beholds Senaka of noble wisdom;
are you one who has cast off the veil, a seer of all?”
“O Brahmin, do you have the wisdom to discern what is fearful?
“I have these seven hundred [oxen];
take them all, I give them to you.”
"Indeed, by her I have obtained life today;
she has also brought safety to my wife.
"The wise do not accept wages," [he said].
With variegated verses well-spoken;
from this too, O Brahmā, let them give you wealth.
Taking it, go to your own abode.”
The Sattubhastajātaka is the seventh.
